$comment: Notes for translators, keyed by message identifier. They explain wording that is ambiguous out of context and are not shown in the application.
scale_controls_one_batch: A batch is one full quantity of the recipe as written. Two batches means doubling it.
scale_controls_batch_size: How many times the written recipe to make, not the size of a baking tray.
plan_batch: How many times the written recipe is made for this meal.
cooking_ingredients_batch: {value1} is a multiplier of the written recipe, such as 2 or 1½.
cooking_log_batch: {value1} is a multiplier of the written recipe. The leading dot separates it from the date before it.
print_controls_batch: How many times the written recipe the printout is scaled to.
import_job_page_batch_of: Here a batch is a group of files processed together during an import, not a quantity of food.
import_job_stopping: A batch here is a group of files being imported.
quantity_field_no_measure: An amount with a number and no unit.
measurement_decisions_convention_legend: A measure is a unit word, such as cup or tablespoon, whose size differs between countries.
measurement_decisions_read_these_as: {measure} is a unit word from the recipe, such as “cup”.
body_source_updated: The website or book the recipe came from has changed since it was saved.
source_fields_source: Where the recipe came from: a website, book, or person. Not source code.
library_filters_needs_ingredient_review: Recipes with ingredient lines that were read automatically and should be checked by a person.
import_candidate_yield: How much the recipe makes, such as 4 servings or 12 muffins.
editor_yield_wording: How much the recipe makes, in the recipe's own words.
recipe_card_active: Active time is the time the cook is working, as opposed to waiting while something rests or bakes.
recipe_card_active_and_total: Active time is hands-on work; total time includes waiting.
recipe_card_also_in: {languages} is a list of language names written in their own languages, such as “Français and العربية”.
recipe_card_also_matches_in: The search also found this recipe in these other languages. {languages} is a list of language names.
body_about_amount: {amount} is a formatted quantity with its unit, such as “2 cups”.
translations_relation_alternate: The two recipes are the same dish in different languages, and neither is known to be the original. Not a duplicate.
translations_relation_original: The recipe this one was translated from.
translations_relation_translation: A recipe translated from this one.
translations_relation_choice_alternate: An option for how an existing recipe relates to this one.
preferences_light: A light interface color scheme, not a low-calorie recipe.
preferences_dark: A dark interface color scheme, not a dark dish.
translations_unlink: Removes the link between two recipes. Both recipes are kept.
translations_copy_content: Copies the recipe's text as a starting point. The copies are not kept in step afterwards.
translations_languages: Label before the list of languages this recipe is available in.
preferences_interface_preview: {language} is the name of an interface language whose translation is incomplete or not yet reviewed.
common_dot_separator: Separates short items on one line. Use the separator your language uses between list items in a caption.
recipe_compare_keep_my_edit: When a recipe's source has changed, keep this part as you edited it.
recipe_compare_use_source: When a recipe's source has changed, take this part from the updated source instead of your edit.
organization_label_book: A recipe book: a collection in the library, shown beside the recipe's tags.
duration_about: {duration} is a length of time such as 10 min.
duration_at_least: {duration} is a length of time such as 10 min.
recipe_article_written_total_shorter: {value1} is the total time the recipe's author wrote, such as 6 hr 15 min. Savorum does not show it as the recipe's time because the steps add up to more.
organization_summary_not_filed_yet: Said of the recipe being read: the library has not filed it under any book, tag or category. The recipe's own categories from its source are separate.
page_title_named: A browser tab title. {name} is a recipe or book title, or a page heading.
page_title_cooking: A browser tab title while cooking. {name} is the recipe title.
page_title_editing: A browser tab title while editing. {name} is the recipe title.
cooking_add_recipe: While cooking: add another recipe to cook at the same time, as another dish of the meal.
plan_new_meal_on: The accessible name of the add button on one day of the plan. {date} is a weekday and date, such as Monday, September 21.
plan_keep_meal: Undoes Skip this meal, so a skipped meal is planned as usual again.
shopping_source_dated: Where shopping ingredients came from. {date} is the day a meal is planned, such as Thu, Sep 24; {label} is the dish or meal name.
shopping_from_plan: Opens the meal plan to choose meals whose ingredients go on the shopping list.
editor_add_row_shortcut: Shown when pointing at the button that adds an ingredient or step. The keys add a row after the one being typed in.
account_admin_person_self: Shown on the administrator's own row in the list of people, followed by a link to Sign-in and security.
account_admin_library_none: A choice for the library a new account joins: do not add the account to a library now.
recipe_article_also_makes: {yields} lists the recipe's other stated amounts, such as "about 600 g · 6 servings".
scale_controls_scale_by_yield: {yields} is one stated amount, such as "24 cookies"; scaling changes the batch to make more or fewer of it.
nutrition_basis_serving_of: {serving} is the source's own serving size wording, such as "1 slice".
nutrition_recipe_value: Shown after a scaled whole-recipe value; {value} is the value the recipe itself states.
claims_condition: {condition} is the source's own qualification, such as "when made with plant-based milk".
claims_for_variant: {variant} is the title of one of the recipe's variations.
claims_free_from: Label before substances the source declares absent, as in "Free from peanuts".
claims_editor_presence: Label for a choice between Contains, May contain, and Free from.
library_query_stated_diet: A search filter chip; {diet} is a diet such as Vegan, stated by the recipe's source.
library_query_stated_free_from: A search filter chip; {substance} is typed by the reader, such as peanuts.
dependency_see: After an ingredient made by another recipe; {recipe} is that recipe's title.
media_details_credit: The credit line a source prints with a photo, such as "Photo: Jane Smith".
editor_name_group: A short title for one group of ingredients, such as For the sauce. The button adds the title field.
editor_name_stage: A short title for one stage of the method, such as For the sauce. The button adds the title field.
editor_more_details: Heading above the recipe's optional details: nutrition, dietary statements, source and keywords.
ingredient_row_line_example: A sample ingredient line shown in an empty ingredient field: an amount, a unit, the ingredient, and a note after a comma. Write it the way a cook writes an ingredient in this language, with this language's unit words and word order, because the field reads what is typed with the same rules.
creation_retry_reconcile: Shown when a creation request is too old to retry safely. The reader checks the library before submitting a new request.
creation_retry_allow_new: Button confirming that the reader checked whether an expired creation request succeeded and permits a new submission.
account_assistant_setup_prompt: Machine-facing bootstrap instructions, intentionally in English to match the instance guide. This prompt contains no credentials.
account_assistant_check_code: The user compares this short code with the code their assistant displays before approving a device authorization request.
status_loading_slow: Shown after ten seconds of initial loading.
plan_meal_tray: The area beside the calendar for unscheduled and saved meals.
library_sort_cooked: Sort recipes by the most recent cooking record first.
shopping_arrange: Enables in-list reordering and selecting items to combine.
recipe_from_source_page: Disclosure for authored categories, keywords, and dates copied from the source page, at the end of recipe instructions.
import_job_timing: Collapsed disclosure containing the start time, elapsed duration, and finish time of a completed import.
ingredient_unit: Accessible label for choosing the display unit of one ingredient. This changes the reading, not the stored recipe.
keyboard_shortcuts_enabled: Checkbox that enables or disables character keyboard shortcuts. Keep the label brief; other platform keyboard commands are unaffected.
help_plan: Accessible name and tooltip of the meal-planning guide link. A complete phrase, not a prefix.
help_shopping: Accessible name and tooltip of the shopping-list guide link. Refers to the Shopping feature, not a list name.
help_imports: Accessible name and tooltip of the recipe-import guide link.
account_admin_create_heading: Title and primary action for an administrator adding a person with a login name and password. The supporting text explains password sign-in; avoid technical terms such as local account in the title.
account_admin_manage_named: Accessible name and dialog title for managing one user. {name} is the user display name.
account_passkeys_rename_named: Accessible label for renaming one passkey. {name} is the name chosen by the user.
account_admin_reset_action: Button that resets another user’s password. The consequence is explained next to the field.
account_admin_reset_hint: Password-reset helper text for an administrator managing another user.
account_audit_details: Disclosure for exact identifiers and outcome in an immutable audit record.
account_audit_by: Audit table column and filter for the person or service that performed an event.
account_audit_affected: Type of object affected by an audit event, such as an account or recipe.
account_audit_sign_in: Activity name, a noun, for an attempted sign-in. Its result is shown separately.
